original_statement: Deterministic CDE encoding of signing-path values: the same value always encodes to the same bytes — CDE bytewise-lex map ordering (never length-first), shortest integers, no indefinite lengths, no floats
restatement: Any value the module encodes for a signing payload must always produce exactly one byte sequence: (s1) encoding the same value twice, in any construction order, always yields identical bytes; (s2) map keys serialize in bytewise-lexicographic order of their encoded bytes, never sorted by key length first, regardless of insertion order; (s3) integers always use the shortest valid encoding for their value, with no non-canonical padding; (s4) the encoder never emits indefinite-length markers or floating-point values on the signing path.

goal: A committed CDE implementation in the module core where any value maps to exactly one byte sequence — bytewise-lex map ordering, shortest-form integers, no indefinite-length items, no floats — verified by golden test vectors (the P0 exit bar in docs/02-implementation-plan.md).

acceptance_tests.proves: An encoder with any hidden nondeterminism (unstable map/struct iteration, non-reproducible handling) is caught on re-encoding the same value.
acceptance_tests.description: Encoding the same value twice, in any construction order, always yields identical bytes.

acceptance_tests.proves: Across the explored space of key-insertion permutations for the same map content, every reachable state yields byte-identical output whose key order matches the bytewise-lex sort of each key's own encoded bytes — order is a canonical function of content, never of insertion order or key length. Canonical map ordering is a claim over ALL permutations, so exploring the permutation space is the honest oracle; the prior pairwise comparison undertested it.
acceptance_tests.description: Map keys serialize in bytewise-lexicographic order of their encoded bytes, never sorted by key length first, regardless of insertion order.

acceptance_tests.proves: An encoder that zero-pads or picks a wider-than-necessary integer width is caught at a magnitude-boundary value, where encoded length exceeds the canonical minimum.
acceptance_tests.description: Integers always use the shortest valid encoding for their value, with no non-canonical padding.

acceptance_tests.proves: An encoder that silently falls back to a non-canonical form for an indefinite-length or float input is caught — it must reject such inputs outright rather than encode them.
acceptance_tests.description: The encoder never emits indefinite-length markers or floating-point values on the signing path.
